title: The deliberate-buy arming test proves the three arming calls happen inside one process, but the only production caller is a script that exits right after the buy, so the registered S0 (deliberate buy left unprotected) passes it green

evidence.note: startExitMonitor, snapshotLpBaseline and registerAntiRugPosition are spies that resolve at once
case (a) asserts the three calls and their arguments; nothing observes a running monitor
the production caller runs executeDeliberateBuy and then process.exit(0)
armPositionMonitoring awaits startExitMonitor; the monitor is an in-process interval
startExitMonitor returns without arming when the first quote fails (AUD-EXIT-002); the spy cannot show it

sibling_sites_checked: Other tests of deliberate-buy protection: bot/deliberateBuyAffordability (gate only), bot/noDoubleBuyReconcile (no-double-buy guard only). No unit or integration-scope test in the TESTU slice runs scripts/deliberate-buy.ts.
severity_rationale: S2: the file header claims it closes the "held position left UNMONITORED / RUG-UNPROTECTED" harm, while the registered S0 AUD-BUY-001 (that same harm, through the script lifetime) and the S1 AUD-EXIT-002 pass it green.
recommendation: Phase 28 (after the Phase 24 fix for AUD-BUY-001): test the protection where it must live, for example that a landed deliberate buy is recorded so the main bot's restart scan arms it, or that the script hands the position to a running bot; keep the arming-call test as a unit check only.
affected_cases: (a) public-fallback landed buy ARMS startExitMonitor + snapshotLpBaseline + registerAntiRugPosition (resolved tradeId + V2 pair + deliberate amount)
(b) private-landed buy ARMS the same monitoring trio
(c) late-land included buy (no-double-buy guard reconciles included) ARMS the same monitoring trio
(e) anti-rug baseline failure (snapshotLpBaseline throws) STILL arms the exit monitor + logs antirug.baseline-snapshot-failed
escaped_regression: Today's code already escapes (AUD-BUY-001): scripts/deliberate-buy.ts:150 calls process.exit(0) right after the buy, so the monitor dies with the process, and every case stays green. A concrete code change that also stays green: make startExitMonitor return before registerExitMonitor for any reason (as it does at src/exitEngine.ts:1870-1872 on a failed quote); the spy still records one call.
